zh: 第3章 古典原子论
en: Chapter 3. CLASSICAL ATOMISM

zh: 在蒸汽机发明之前，力学和机械论世界观建立在阿基米德的简单机械之上。这些机械可以通过几何学进行数学分析。阿基米德的著作提供了这种分析，以杠杆为核心范例，并把其他机械视为杠杆的推广。
en: Before the steam engine’s invention, mechanics and the mechanical world view were based on Archimedes’ simple machines. These machines were amenable to mathematical analysis through geometry. Archimedes’ works provided this analysis, with levers as the central example, viewing other machines as lever generalizations.

zh: 原子论唯物主义认为，现实的基本构成单元是物质粒子，被称为原子、corpora 或其他名称。机械唯物主义在此基础上进一步主张，物质遵循严格的守恒定律。卢克莱修阐述了“无中不能生有”原则；尽管在他那里这属于哲学语境，但在机械唯物主义中，该原则通过守恒定律和对称性获得了精确表达。
en: Atomistic materialism posits that the fundamental constituents of reality are particles of matter, referred to as atoms, corpora or other terms. Mechanical materialism builds on this by stating that matter adheres to strict conservation laws. Lucretius elaborated the principle ‘nothing comes from nothing’, which, although philosophical in his context, is given precise expression in mechanical materialism through conservation laws and symmetries.

zh: 阿基米德
古代思想家中，现存著作最清晰地表达这种机械唯物主义的是阿基米德
。他在《论平面的平衡》开篇写道：
en: The ancient thinker whose surviving works expressed this most clearly is Archimedes,
who opened his book
as follows:

zh: 我提出以下公设：
en: I POSTULATE the following:

zh: 1. 等距的等重物处于平衡；不等距的等重物不平衡，而是向距离较远的重物倾斜。2. 如果当位于特定距离的重物处于平衡时，向其中一个重物添加某物，它们便不再平衡，而是向被添加重物的一侧倾斜。3. 同样，如果从其中一个重物取走某物，它们便不再平衡，而是向未被取走重物的一侧倾斜。
en: 1. Equal weights at equal distances are in equilibrium, and equal weights at unequal distances are not in equilibrium but incline towards the weight which is at the greater distance. 2. If, when weights at certain distances are in equilibrium, something be added to one of the weights, they are not in equilibrium but incline towards the weight to which the addition was made. 3. Similarly, if anything be taken away from one of the weights, they are not in equilibrium but incline towards the weight from which nothing was taken.

zh: 原理（1）陈述了一条守恒定律：支点两侧的距离与重量之积必须守恒。他后来更明确地表述为：
en: Principle (1) states a conservation law that the distance times weight on each side of the fulcrum must be conserved. He later states this more explicitly as:

zh: 两个量，无论是否可通约，当它们与支点的距离与这两个量成反比时，便处于平衡。
en: Two magnitudes, whether commensurable or incommensurable, balance at distances reciprocally proportional to the magnitudes.

zh: 原理（2）和（3）在这一语境中表达了 ex nihilo nihil fit（无中不能生有）原则：若不向处于平衡状态的物体添加物质，或从中移除物质，就不会产生运动。
en: Principles (2) and (3) express the
principle in the context that without the addition (or subtraction) of matter from an equilibrium position, there will be no motion.

zh: 我们略过了他详细分析各种几何形状重心所需的其他命题。他运用古典几何技术证明了一些命题，例如：“在任何三角形中，重心位于连接任意一个角与对边中点的直线上。”然而，在著作的其他部分，他使用了看似极为现代的技术：递归分解以及实质上属于积分的方法。过去两千年来孩子们不得不背诵的一些公式——圆的面积
和球体面积
——最初正是由他使用这些技术发现的。他最初把圆面积公式表述为：
en: We have missed other propositions, which he needed in order to make detailed analyses of the centres of gravity of various geometrical shapes. He proves some propositions, like: ‘In any triangle the centre of gravity lies on the straight line joining any angle to the middle point of the opposite side’ by classical geometrical techniques. In other parts of his work, however, he uses what seem to be remarkably modern techniques: recursive decomposition and what is effectively integration. Some of the formulae that children have had to learn by heart these last two millennia –
for a circle’s area and
for a sphere’s – were first discovered by him using these techniques. The first formula he stated in the form:

zh: 任何圆的面积等于一个直角三角形，其中直角旁的一条边等于半径，另一条边等于圆周长。
en: The area of any circle is equal to a right-angled triangle in which one of the sides about the right angle is equal to the radius, and the other to the circumference.

zh: 阿基米德的方法显示了几何学与力学之间紧密且相互支持的关系。例如，他推导球体体积
时明确使用了力学论证。第一步是证明：一个单位圆柱体的体积等于一个单位半球体与一个单位圆锥体体积之和。
en: Archimedes’ approach shows a close and mutually supportive relationship between geometry and mechanics. For example, his derivation of the volume of a sphere as
uses explicitly mechanical arguments. His first step is to show that a unit cylinder has the same volume as the sum of the volumes of a unit hemisphere plus a unit cone.

zh: 单位圆柱指高和半径均为1 的圆柱。单位圆锥指高和半径均为1 的圆锥。单位半球是半径为1 的半球。
en: A unit cylinder is one whose height and radius are each 1. A unit cone is one whose height and radius are 1. Of course, a unit hemisphere is the hemisphere with a radius of 1.

zh: 他的证明使用了他所谓的“机械法”。假设圆锥、半球和圆柱是由相同材料制成的重物。他断言，如果把它们以等距悬挂在支点两侧，如图3.1 所示，使圆锥和半球在一侧，圆柱在另一侧，那么它们会完全平衡。
en: His proof uses what he called his ‘mechanical method’. Assume that the cone, hemisphere and cylinder are weights made of the same material. He asserts that if we attach them at equal distances from a fulcrum, as shown in Figure 3.1, with the cone and hemisphere on one side and the cylinder on the other, then they will exactly balance.

zh: 图3.1 阿基米德证明，单位圆柱体的体积等于单位圆锥体与单位半球体的体积之和。作者绘图。

en: Figure 3.1 Archimedes proved that a unit cylinder has the same volume as a unit cone and a unit hemisphere. Figure by authors.

zh: 他并不满足于圆锥、球体和圆柱。他进而求抛物线下的面积，为此构想了更复杂的天平装置，把三角形和抛物线下的区域悬挂在支点不同距离处。但为什么他关注抛物线等曲线？
en: He did not content himself with just cones, spheres and cylinders. He moved on to integrate the areas under parabolas, for which proof he imagines more complex arrangements of the balance, with triangles and areas under a parabola suspended at different distances from the fulcrum. But why his concern with curves like parabolas?

zh: 鲁索
认为，阿基米德的研究，尤其是他开创静水力学这一学科，与晚期希腊化文明的经济和政治秩序密切相关。鲁索指出，阿基米德所生活的锡拉库萨的经济和军事目标可以解释这一点。锡拉库萨是一支主要海军力量，致力于建造越来越大的船只。正因如此，阿基米德在静水力学分析中才关注推导浮体的稳定静止角，包括对以抛物线描述的物体如何漂浮的分析。抛物线曲线是可能的船体形状。
en: Russo

argues that Archimedes’ research, particularly his invention of hydrostatics as a discipline, was closely connected to the economic and political order of late Hellenistic civilization. Russo points to the economic and military objectives of Syracuse, the state in which Archimedes lived, as an explanation. Syracuse was a major naval power, striving to build ever larger ships. That is why Archimedes was so concerned in his hydrostatic analysis to derive the angles of stable repose of floating bodies. This included an analysis of how bodies described in terms of parabolas would float. Parabolic curves are possible hull forms.

zh: 抛物线形状已被阿基米德的前辈阿波罗尼乌斯分析为圆锥的截面。绘制和构造此类曲线的方法已为人知。根据这些规则，造船师可以切割出船体的成型肋骨。
en: The parabolic shape had already been analysed by one of Archimedes’ predecessors, Apollonius, as segments of cones. The method of constructing and drawing such curves was understood. From these rules, shipwrights could cut out the forming ribs of a ship’s hull.

zh: 在希腊化时期，相互竞争的商贸国家出于经济和政治原因资助科学研究。阿基米德开创的静水力学新科学由经济和军事需求驱动，他利用它推导船体所能承受的最大稳定载荷。然而，罗马征服终结了科学资助，阿基米德也被杀。一个统一国家在地中海地区的建立，切断了科学研究的资金来源。17 世纪，法国科学院和英国皇家学会在相互竞争的海上贸易经济推动下，恢复了对科学的国家资助。
en: During the Hellenistic period, competing merchant states funded scientific research for economic and political reasons. Archimedes’ new science of hydrostatics was driven by economic and military necessity, and he used it to deduce the maximum stable load that hulls could bear. However, the Roman conquest ended funding for science, and Archimedes was famously killed. The establishment of a single state over the inland sea removed the sources of funding for science. The French Academy and British Royal Society resumed state funding of science in the seventeenth century, driven again by the existence of mercantile sea-borne trading economies in mutual competition.

zh: 在上述阿基米德的证明中，他利用等价性推导球体性质。但数学中的这种等价性论证依赖关于力学的先前的公理。这些公理又假设力学定律本身由等价关系定义。
en: In Archimedes’ proof above, he is using equivalence to deduce the properties of the sphere. But this equivalence argument in maths is relying on prior axioms about mechanics. These in turn assume that mechanical laws themselves are defined in terms of equivalence relations.

zh: 这也适用于他在流体静力学方面那些更为人熟知的发现。这里的关键定律是：漂浮物体排开与自身等重的液体；浸没物体则排开与自身等体积的液体，这比它自身的重量要小。我们在这里再次遇到体积的相等与重量的相等，这正是上述证明的主题。
en: The same applies to his much better-known discoveries in hydrostatics. The key laws here are that a floating body displaces its own weight of liquid, whereas one that is submerged displaces its own volume of liquid, this being less than its own weight. Here again we have equivalences of volumes and equivalences of weights, the themes in the proof we have run through.
body.review: 底本“this being less than its own weight”指代不清，字面上混用了体积与重量。若指下沉物体所排液体的重量小于物体重量，则需限定密度条件；正文保留其原有表述。

zh: 阿基米德用于确定质心和浮力的几何证明方法需要极高巧思和深刻理解，今天很少有人能掌握。我们改用有限元方法，本质上是数值积分，作为替代。然而，没有电子计算工具，几何学仍是解决这些问题的少数工具之一。在古典几何中，一方面有机械性的物质过程：绘制直线和相交圆；另一方面有用有理数进行的实际计算，阿基米德为
设定的明确数值界限就是例证。让我们稍作思考。
en: Archimedes’ geometrical proof methods for determining centres of mass and buoyancy demand ingenuity and depth of understanding that few can master today. Instead, we use finite element methods, essentially numerical integration, as a substitute. However, without electronic computational aids, geometry remains one of the only tools to solve these problems. With classical geometry, there is on the one hand a mechanical material process: the drawing of straight lines and intersecting circles; on the other hand, there is actual calculation in terms of rational numbers, as exemplified by the explicit numerical bounds Archimedes set for π. Let us reflect for a bit on what is involved here.

zh: 假设你是一位建造神庙的建筑师。你用木炭绘制图纸，也许在纸莎草纸上，也许在白色大理石板上。这些图纸构成未来神庙的物质模型。

图纸用直尺和圆规等机械工具绘制。但假设图纸只使用这些工具绘制，长度由例如“正方形面积加倍法”或黄金比例矩形确定。那么你也知道最终神庙的大致线性尺寸。这些尺寸也以比例形式存在，最终可从毕达哥拉斯定理推导，这些比例必然存在于设计元素的长度之间。理论几何学确立了缩尺图纸上必然近似的测量值与最终建筑更精确的相对尺寸之间的相似性。根据所需精度，可以一边放大比例一边重复相同构造，仍使用直线和圆。直线可以通过立柱的视觉对齐标记，大圆可以用锚定在固定点的绷紧链条描绘。
en: Suppose you were an architect constructing a temple. You draw plans in charcoal, perhaps on papyrus or perhaps on a white marble slab. These plans constitute a material model of the temple to come.

The plans are drawn with mechanical aids, ruler and compass. But suppose the drawing is one made using just these tools, with lengths set by, for example, the ‘square doubling technique’ or the drawing of a rectangle in the Golden Ratio. In that case, you also know the approximate linear dimensions of the final temple. These will also be in ratios, ultimately derivable from Pythagoras’ theorem, that must exist between the lengths of the elements of the design. The theoretical geometry establishes a similarity between the necessarily approximate measurements on the scale drawing and the much more precise relative dimensions of the final building. Depending on the accuracy required, the same constructions can be done while increasing scales, again using straight lines and circles. Straight lines can be marked by visual alignment of posts and large circles traced out with taut chains anchored to a fixed point.

zh: 机械唯物主义使一种物质系统——平面图——能够作为另一种物质系统——神庙——的模型。二者都是物质。平面图与建筑之间的相似性，通过在放大比例上重复相同构造步骤得到保证。所构建的图像既是客观知识，也是建筑的目的（telos）。物理建模过程使众多工匠能够协调合作，每人建造子组件、立柱、基座等，其各自尺寸由黄金比例协调。
en: Mechanical materialism allows one material system, the plan, to act as a model for another, the temple. Both are material. The similarity between plan and building is assured by the repetition of the same constructive steps on an enlarged scale. The constructed image is both objective knowledge and

of the building. The physical modelling process allows the coordination of the multiple craft workers, each constructing subcomponents, pillars, plinths etc., whose individual dimensions are coordinated by golden ratios.

zh: 古代唯物主义者对原子论的批评

children: Criticism of atomism by ancient materialists

zh: 古代存在不认同原子论的唯物主义者。原子论虽然根本有效，但在古典时期失去了公信力。这是因为它试图解释一些对当时粗浅原子论来说过于复杂的现象。伊壁鸠鲁知道静电和磁现象。他知道摩擦过的琥珀棒会吸引灰尘和谷壳，磁石会吸引铁。
en: In ancient times, there existed materialists who did not subscribe to atomism. The atomic theory, which is fundamentally valid, suffered a loss of credibility during the classical era. This was due to its attempts to account for phenomena that were far too complex for the rudimentary form of atomism available at the time. Epicurus knew of electrostatic and magnetic phenomena. He knew that a rubbed amber rod would attract dust and chaff. He knew that lodestone attracted iron.

zh: 他对此的解释是：起吸引作用的物体（琥珀或磁石）释放出微小粒子，其大小比其他物质的原子小一万倍。这些更小的原子形状特殊，会与被吸引物体缠绕，把二者结合。
en: He interpreted this in terms of the attracting object (the amber or lodestone) emitting tiny particles, ten thousand times smaller than the atoms of other things. The shapes of these tinier atoms were such that they became entangled with the object being attracted and bound the two together.

zh: 我们现在知道，静电吸引确实涉及更小粒子：琥珀摩擦时发生电子转移。电子确实比构成琥珀的原子轻数万倍。但在没有正负电荷概念和超距作用力概念时，伊壁鸠鲁学派的解释似乎不可信。应用于磁学时更不可思议。
en: We now know that electrostatic attraction does involve tinier particles: electrons being transferred when amber is rubbed. An electron is indeed of the order of tens of thousands of times lighter than the atoms making up the amber. But without the notion of positive and negative charge and without the notion of action-at-a-distance forces, the Epicurean explanation seemed implausible. Applied to magnetism, it was still more incredible.

zh: 原子论是古典罗马医学中的重要哲学流派，主要由阿斯克勒皮亚德斯倡导。这一观点认为，疾病源于允许分子循环的微小体孔收缩或扩张。如果体孔收缩，疾病被归类为“停滞”；如果扩张，则被归类为“流溢”。
en: Atomism was a significant philosophical approach in classical Roman medicine, chiefly advocated by Asclepiades. This perspective suggested that diseases resulted from the constriction or dilation of tiny body pores that allowed molecules to circulate. Diseases were classified as ‘stasis’ if the pores were constricted and as ‘flux’ if they were dilated.

zh: 该假说并非完全荒谬，因为现代医学仍承认血管收缩和血管扩张可能是病理现象。但应用于解剖细节时，它可能变得荒谬。阿斯克勒皮亚德斯认为，水通过膀胱壁上不可见的微小通道从血液进入膀胱。
en: The hypothesis was not totally absurd, since modern medicine still recognizes vaso-constriction and vaso-dilation as possible pathologies. But when applied to the details of anatomy, it could become absurd. Asclepiades held that water passed from the blood into the bladder via invisible tiny channels in the wall of the bladder.

zh: 另一位医学导师盖伦是解剖学专家，他轻而易举地驳斥了这些关于膀胱的说法。他描述了活体解剖实验，证明膀胱通过输尿管流入尿液而充盈：
en: A rival medical teacher, Galen, who was an expert on anatomy, had no difficulty in refuting these claims about the bladder. He describes vivisection experiments which demonstrated that the bladder was filled via a flow of urine through the ureters.

zh: 现在，证明方法如下。必须切开输尿管前方的腹膜，然后用结扎线固定输尿管，接着给动物包扎好，再放它走（因为它不会继续排尿）。此后，松开外部绷带，显示膀胱是空的，而输尿管完全充盈并膨胀——事实上几乎要破裂；解开输尿管结扎线后，便可清楚看到膀胱充盈尿液。
en: Now the method of demonstration is as follows. One has to divide the peritoneum in front of the ureters, then secure these with ligatures, and next, having bandaged up the animal, let him go (for he will not continue to urinate). After this one loosens the external bandages and shows the bladder empty and the ureters quite full and distended – in fact almost on the point of rupturing; on removing the ligature from them, one then plainly sees the bladder becoming filled with urine.

zh: 在从解剖学上批判伊壁鸠鲁学派后，盖伦接着质疑他们对静电和磁吸引的解释。他说，伊壁鸠鲁认为铁被磁石吸引，谷壳被琥珀吸引。他解释说，从磁石流出的原子容易与从铁流出的原子相互交织，导致缠结和吸引。尽管假说缺乏说服力，伊壁鸠鲁承认吸引存在。但很难相信磁石粒子能吸引铁。即使接受这一点，仍无法解释为什么铁会粘在另一块铁上。这是如何发生的？
en: Having criticized the Epicureans on anatomical grounds, Galen then goes on to cast doubt on their explanations of electrostatic and magnetic attraction. Epicurus, he said, believes that iron is attracted to the lodestone and chaff to amber. He explains that the atoms flowing from the stone easily interlock with those flowing from the iron, causing entanglement and attraction. Despite his unconvincing hypotheses, Epicurus acknowledges the existence of attraction. But it’s hard to believe that particles from a lodestone can attract iron. Even if we accept this, it still doesn’t explain why iron sticks to other iron. How does this happen?

zh: 粒子与铁碰撞后反弹，使铁悬浮吗？还是它们穿透铁块，与另一块铁碰撞而无法穿透？然后它们回到第一块铁，像之前那样造成缠结吗？
en: Do the particles collide with the iron and bounce back, suspending it? Or do they penetrate the iron and collide with another piece without being able to pass through? Then do they return to the first piece and cause entanglements like before?

zh: 这一假说因其荒谬而被明确驳斥：事实上，我曾见过五根铁制书写针成一排相互附着，只有第一根与磁石接触，而磁力通过它传递给其余几根。此外，不能说如果把第二根铁笔与第一根下端接触，它就被固定、附着并悬停；而如果接触针身侧面任何其他部位，它却不会附着。因为磁石的力量向四面八方扩散；它只需在任何一点与第一根针接触；力量便从这根针出发，快如思想般流经第二根，再从第二根流向第三根。现在，试想一块小磁石悬挂在屋内，其四周接触大量铁片，这些铁片又连接其他铁片，这些铁片再连接其他铁片，如此类推——所有这些铁片必然充满从磁石散发的微粒；因此，这块小磁石很可能因分解为这些散发物而消散。
en: The hypothesis here becomes clearly refuted by its absurdity. As a matter of fact, I have seen five writing-stylets of iron attached to one another in a line, only the first one being in contact with the lodestone, and the power being transmitted through it to the others. Moreover, it cannot be said that if you bring a second stylet into contact with the lower end of the first, it becomes held, attached, and suspended, whereas, if you apply it to any other part of the side it does not become attached. For the power of the lodestone is distributed in all directions; it merely needs to be in contact with the first stylet at any point; from this stylet again the power flows, as quick as a thought, all through the second, and from that again to the third. Now, if you imagine a small lodestone hanging in a house, and in contact with it all round a large number of pieces of iron, from them again others, from these others, and so on,—all these pieces of iron must surely become filled with the corpuscles which emanate from the stone; therefore, this first little stone is likely to become dissipated by disintegrating into these emanations.

zh: 直到20 世纪中叶，人们才真正理解铁的磁性。正确理解磁性需要一系列进一步进展：超距作用力、法拉第对电与磁现象的统一，以及电子和电子自旋的发现。
en: The magnetism of iron was not understood until the mid-twentieth century. A proper understanding of magnetism required a whole set of further advances: action-at-a-distance forces, Faraday’s unification of electric and magnetic phenomena and the discovery of electrons and electron spin.

zh: 盖伦致力于推广一种与之竞争的唯物主义生理学理论，允许物质相互转化。他认为食物通过肝门静脉的一种能力转化为血液。他嘲笑“面包中包含肉和骨的元素”这一说法，主张身体具有转化物质的能力。
en: Galen was concerned to promote a rival materialist theory of physiology which allowed transformation of substances, one into another. He believed that food was converted into blood via a faculty of the hepatic portal vein. He ridiculed the notion that bread contained within it the elements of flesh and bone, arguing instead that it was a faculty of the body to transmute substances.

zh: 盖伦认为，神经以气动方式工作。这一理论最早由埃拉西斯特拉图斯提出，他认为神经中有空腔，精神之气（psychic pneuma）
从中通过。气压沿神经传导，使肌肉膨胀并由此收缩。盖伦与埃拉西斯特拉图斯在生理学上都相信“气”（pneuma）的作用。吸入的空气在肺中转化为生命之气（vital pneuma），与血液混合并到达脑部。在那里，它被转化为精神之气，即“动物精气”（spiritus animalis），调节脑与神经的功能。
en: Galen believed that the nerves worked pneumatically. This was a theory initially advanced by Erasistratus, who held that nerves contain a cavity through which

passed. That air pressure was transmitted down the nerves and caused muscles to expand and thus contract. Galen and Erasistratus believed in ‘pneuma’ in physiology. Inhaling air transforms into vital pneuma in the lungs that mixes with blood and reaches the brain. It’s converted into
, ‘spiritus animalis’, which regulates brain and nerve function.

zh: 生命依赖空气这一点显而易见。如果动物鼻孔和嘴巴被堵住，它就会窒息。他的解剖实验证明，如果切断神经，被解剖动物在该神经支配区域就失去运动能力。此外，古人懂得制造气动装置，甚至简单气动自动机。气动技术是那个时代的先进技术。
en: That life depended on air was clear. If an animal had its nose and mouth stopped, it suffocated. His dissection experiments had demonstrated that if he cut a nerve, the animal he was dissecting lost the power of movement in the area supplied by the nerve. Moreover, the ancients knew how to build pneumatically powered machines, or even simple pneumatic automata. Pneumatics was the advanced technology of the age.

zh: 盖伦的唯物主义为天主教话语中的唯心主义主题奠定基础。他否认不朽灵魂存在，认为意识取决于大脑。在随后的基督教时期，一种经过修改的理论出现：不朽精神栖息于大脑脑室，赋予身体生命。这把原本的唯物主义理论转变为其对立面。
en: Galen’s materialism formed the basis for idealistic themes in Catholic discourse. He denied the existence of an immortal soul and believed that consciousness depended on the brain. In the Christian period that followed, a modified theory emerged, stating that the immortal spirit resided in the brain’s ventricles, animating the body. This transformed the original materialist theory into its opposite.

zh: 不再认为动物精气由身体从吸入肺部的物质空气（pneuma）制造，而是《天主教教理》声称：
en: Instead of the animal spirit being manufactured by the body from the material air (pneuma) inspired into the lungs, we get the Catholic Catechism stating:

zh: 基督教关于人的观点——人按上帝形象被造，既有灵性灵魂又有肉体——具有核心重要性。灵魂是我们内心承载的永恒之种，不能仅归结为物质，其起源只能来自上帝。
en: The Christian vision of the human person made in the image of God with a spiritual soul as well as a body is of central importance. The soul, the seed of eternity we bear in ourselves, irreducible to the merely material, can have its origin only in God.

zh: 人体之所以是人，恰恰因为它被灵性灵魂赋予生命。
en: The human body is human precisely because it is animated by a spiritual soul.

zh: 基督教教义是过去实验科学被扭曲的记忆或被误解的遗迹。spiritus（盖伦 pneuma 的拉丁译名）原本的气力机械含义完全丧失。这个词脱离原义，变成完全抽象的概念，神学家便可随意赋予它想象属性。
en: The Christian doctrine is the distorted memory or misunderstood relic of a past experimental science. The actual pneumatic mechanical meaning of spiritus (Latin translation of Galen’s pneuma) is totally lost. The word, detached from its original real meaning, became something entirely abstract, to which the theologians became free to attach any imaginary properties.

zh: 牛顿
在牛顿时代，若有人提及古典思想家，指的是希腊人和罗马人。如今，随时间流逝，牛顿被视为机械唯物主义的典范哲学家，以至于“经典力学”和“牛顿力学”实际上成为同义词。
en: In Newton’s day, if someone referred to the classical thinkers, they meant the Greeks and the Romans. Now, with the passage of time, Newton is seen as the archetypal philosopher of mechanical materialism, so much so that the terms
and
have effectively become synonymous.

zh: 通过卢克莱修，宇宙由不断运动的粒子构成的观念在古典文明衰落后存续。通过阿基米德，后来被称为静力学的理论也存续。我们现在知道，阿基米德还发展了非常接近微积分的数学技术。但让我们了解这些内容的手稿直到19 世纪末才印刷出版。鲁索
推测，也许牛顿接触过这部及其他后来因霉变和腐朽失传的古典文献。无论推测是否属实，微分学正是通过牛顿和莱布尼茨传播的。牛顿把力学从静止物体科学转变为运动物体科学。
en: Via Lucretius, the idea of a universe made up of constantly moving particles had survived the fall of classical civilization. Via Archimedes, what later came to be known as static mechanics had also survived. We now know that Archimedes had also developed mathematical techniques very close to calculus. But the manuscript by which we know these things was not published in print till the late nineteenth century. Russo

speculated that perhaps Newton had access to this and other classical texts, which, through mould and decay, have subsequently been lost to us. Whatever the truth of these speculations, it is via Newton and Leibniz that the differential calculus was subsequently promulgated. Newton transformed mechanics from a science of static bodies to one of moving bodies.

zh: 哲学的任务
牛顿把哲学任务阐述如下：
en: Newton sets out the task of philosophy as follows:

zh: 我们提供这部著作作为哲学的数学原理；因为哲学的全部困难似乎在于：从运动现象出发探究自然力，再从这些力出发证明其他现象。

children: We offer this work as the mathematical principles of philosophy; for all the difficulty of philosophy seems to consist in this – from the phænomena of motions to investigate the forces of nature, and then from these forces to demonstrate the other phænomena;

zh: 从运动观察出发，从中推断力和运动定律。这使你能够审视新情况并预测将发生什么。每一艘抵达火星或木星的太空探测器都证实这一方法。
en: Start with observations of motion. Infer from these the forces and laws of motion. This allows you to look at new situations and predict what will occur. Every space probe arriving at Mars or Jupiter confirms this approach.

zh: 我们注意到，卢克莱修的原子论也基于对经验可观察现象的演绎。作为诗人，这些推论自然流露于叙述；作为哲学家，牛顿将其系统化为四条明确推理规则：
en: We noted that Lucretius also based his atomism on deductions from what was empirically observable. As a poet, these simply come out in the telling. As a philosopher, Newton systematized this in a set of four explicit rules of reasoning, which we quote below:

zh: 规则 I
en: RULE I

zh: 对于自然事物，我们承认的原因不应多于既能解释其现象又真实且充分的原因。

children: We are to admit no more causes of natural things than such as are both time and sufficient to explain their appearances.

body.review: 本书英文底本此处作 time，语义不通；中文按上下文采用“真实”，英文仍照录 time，未将校正混入底本文字。

zh: 为此，哲学家们说自然不做无用之事，当较少原因足够时，更多原因就是无用；因为自然喜欢简单，不追求多余原因的浮华。
en: To this purpose, the philosophers say that Nature does nothing in vain, and more is in vain when less will serve, for Nature is pleased with simplicity and affects not the pomp of superfluous causes.

zh: 这就是俗称的KISS 原则：Keep It Simple, Stupid（笨蛋，保持简单）。在此之前，它被称为奥卡姆剃刀：不应在必要原因之外增加实体。牛顿只是重申前辈哲学家的共识：简单解释优于复杂解释。
en: This is what is colloquially called the KISS principle: Keep It Simple, Stupid. Before that, it was known as Occam’s razor, which holds that entities should not be multiplied beyond cause. Here Newton is simply repeating, as he says, the consensus of previous philosophers that simple explanations should always be preferred over complex ones.

zh: 在数学上，这意味着探索自然法则时应优先选择最简单公式，而非更复杂公式。牛顿的同时代人莱布尼茨也持相同观点：
en: In terms of mathematics, this means that we should always prefer the simplest mathematical formula over the more complex when trying to discover a natural law. Leibniz, Newton’s contemporary, argues the same point

zh: 因此，让我们假设，例如，有人像那些从事荒谬地占术（geomancy）的人一样，在纸上随意标出若干点。我认为，完全可能找到一条几何曲线，其运动恒定且均匀，遵循某种规则，使这条曲线按照手写下这些点的顺序依次穿过所有点。
en: Thus, let us assume, for example, that someone jots down a number of points at random on a piece of paper, as do those who practice the ridiculous art of geomancy. I maintain that it is possible to find a geometric line whose motion is constant and uniform, following a certain rule, such that this line passes through all the points in the same order in which the hand jotted them down.

zh: 但当规则极其复杂时，符合该规则的事物便被视为不规则。因此可以说，无论上帝以何种方式创造世界，它始终有规律并符合某种普遍秩序。然而上帝选择了最完美的世界，即在假设上最简单、在现象上最丰富的那一个，正如几何学中一条构造简单但性质与效果极其显著且影响广泛的曲线。
en: But when a rule is extremely complex, what is in conformity with it passes for irregular. Thus, one can say in whatever manner God might have created the world, it would always have been regular and in accordance with a certain general order. But God has chosen the most perfect world, that is, the one which is at the same time the simplest in hypotheses and the richest in phenomena, as might be a line in geometry whose construction is easy and whose properties and effects are extremely remarkable and widespread.

zh: 莱布尼茨打算用何种具体方法，构造一条穿过所有随机点的光滑曲线，并未说明。在18世纪，或许会用如下多项式来拟合这些点：
en: The precise means by which Leibniz intended to construct a smooth curve through all the random points is not specified. In the eighteenth century, perhaps the means would have been to fit a polynomial like

zh: 傅里叶后来发现一种技术，可以用正弦和余弦函数把曲线任意拟合到点上。我们稍后回到这一点。
en: to the points. Fourier would later discover a technique by which you can arbitrarily fit a curve through points using sine and cosine functions. We will return to this.

zh: 牛顿能举出的最明显的例子，是他的太阳系解释比托勒密简单得多。
en: The most obvious example that Newton could invoke in terms of simplicity was how much simpler his explanation of the solar system was than that advocated by Ptolemy.

zh: 用牛顿力学处理太阳系，我们需要每颗行星在时间0 的角动量、半径和旋转相位。运动定律提供其余信息。这意味着每颗行星只需三个数。我忽略太阳质量和引力常数，因为假设它们已知，只考虑每颗行星的额外信息。
en: When dealing with the solar system via Newtonian mechanics, we need the angular momentum, radius and rotational phase for each planet at time 0. The laws of motion give us all the rest. This amounts to three numbers per planet. I am disregarding knowledge of the mass of the Sun and the gravitational constant, as I am assuming these are given from the outset and we are just considering the extra information needed for each planet.

zh: 托勒密模型中，每颗行星绕地球旋转，一个均轮上还有一个本轮旋转。因此至少需要两个半径、两个旋转速率和两个初始相位：每颗行星六个数。所需参数数量是牛顿模型的两倍，形成冗余。因此基于信息经济性，牛顿更可取。他的理论还额外能解释彗星运动，而旧天文学没有相关定律。
en: If we take the Ptolemaic model, each planet rotates around the Earth with one cycle upon which one epicycle rotates. So for Ptolemy, we needed at least two radii, two rates of rotation and two starting phases: six numbers per planet. That amounts to a twofold redundancy compared to Newton. So on the grounds of the information economy, Newton was to be preferred. His theory had the added bonus that it could also account for the motion of comets – for which no law had existed in the older astronomy.

zh: 如果允许本轮叠加本轮，原则上可以把观测数据拟合到任意精度。如图3.2 所示，托勒密方法相当于把余弦波相加。我们把它简化为向水平轴的投影。对托勒密天文观测，x 轴是天球黄道360°，他以此为参照绘制行星位置。显然，这与傅里叶分析相同。
信号的傅里叶分解为不同频率余弦波，正是JPEG 和MPEG 等图像压缩方案使用的方法。观看YouTube 视频时，你看到的是托勒密方法在运作。计算机把图像分析为不同旋转速度的“本轮”。视频文件包含这些本轮半径，视频编解码器据此重建原始图像的近似。
en: If we are allowed to add epicycles on epicycles, then it is in principle possible to fit observations, whether of planets or any other data, to any degree of accuracy we want. As Figure 3.2 illustrates, the Ptolemaic approach amounts to adding cosine waves together. We illustrate it as a simple projection down onto the horizontal axis. For Ptolemaic astronomical observations, the x-axis is the 360◦ of the ecliptic in the sky against which he plotted the planetary positions. It is clear that what is going on here is the same as Fourier analysis.

Fourier decomposition of a signal into cosine waves of different frequencies is what image compression schemes like JPEG and MPEG use. When you view a YouTube video, you are seeing the Ptolemaic method in action. A computer has analysed the picture into what amounts to epicycles with different rotational velocities. The video file contains what amounts to the radii of these epicycles, from which the video codec can reconstruct a good approximation of the original image.

zh: 图3.2 具有本轮运动路径的物体，其轨道在x轴上的投影是余弦曲线之和。本轮直径为0.2，转速是大圆的两倍。右图绘出余弦曲线及其和。作者绘图。
cos θ：余弦 θ；0.2 cos 2θ：0.2倍的余弦 2θ；sum：两者之和。坐标数字及θ沿用原图。
en: Figure 3.2 The projection of the orbital of a body with an epicyclic path onto the x-axis is a sum of cosine curves. The epicycle has a diameter of 0.2 and rotates at twice the rate of the large circle. The right-hand graph plots the cosines and their sums. Figure by authors.

zh: 正如莱布尼茨暗示的，我们可以把方法应用于任何数据集。图3.3 应用于石油销量（百万桶）与每桶价格之间的关系。
en: We can, as Leibniz implies, apply the method to any data set we want. Figure 3.3 applies it to the relationship between the number of barrels of oil sold (in millions) and the price per barrel at which they were sold.

zh: 图3.3 一条连续曲线，穿过代表2007年至2016年间所采集的世界石油价格／出货量数据的各点。此曲线用托勒密天文学所用的本轮方法生成。作者绘图。

en: Figure 3.3 A continuous curve that goes through the points representing world oil price/ shipment data sampled between 2007 and 2016. The curve was produced by applying the epicycle method used in Ptolemaic astronomy. Figure by authors.

zh: 但显然，把该公式等同于根据供应量调节油价的定律是荒谬的。该规则“极其复杂”，符合它的数据“不规则”。相比之下，牛顿运动定律简单且规律性极强地应用于天文现象。因此它们被视为真正的自然定律。
en: But it would clearly be absurd to identify this formula with a law regulating the price of oil as a function of quantity supplied. The rule is ‘extremely complex’ and the data in conformity with it is ‘irregular’. In contrast, Newton’s laws of motion are simple and apply with great regularity to astronomical phenomena. As such, they count as real laws of nature.

zh: 规则 II
en: RULE II

zh: 因此，对相同自然效果，必须尽可能赋予相同原因。

children: Therefore to the same natural effects we must, as far as possible, assign the same causes.

zh: 例如人与动物的呼吸；欧洲与美洲的石头下落；烹饪之火与太阳的光；地球与行星上的光反射。
en: As to respiration in a man and in a beast; the descent of stones in Europe and in America; the light of our culinary fire and of the Sun; the reflection of light in the Earth and in the planets.

zh: 例子虽旧且通俗，但这些例子与这一原则仍被接受。根据光谱估算遥远恒星温度时，我们假设那里与地球适用相同黑体辐射定律。天文学家利用地球矿物样本反照率推导小行星成分时，也应用这一原则。
en: The examples are a bit old and homely, but both the examples and the principle are still accepted. When temperatures of distant stars are estimated from their spectra, we assume that the same black body radiation laws apply there as on Earth. When astronomers attempt to deduce the composition of asteroids from their albedo, using the albedos of mineral samples here on Earth, they apply this principle.

zh: 其背后是刻意排除超自然或宗教原因。牛顿的同时代人会明白，这里指阿那克萨戈拉：他最早提出月球是反射太阳光的岩石，太阳本身是燃烧岩石，因这一不敬神的说法被放逐出雅典。牛顿在规则II 中隐含站在古代唯物主义者一边。
en: Underlying it is the deliberate exclusion of supernatural or religious causes. Newton’s contemporaries would have understood that reference was being made to Anaxagoras, who first posited that the Moon was a rock reflecting light of the Sun, itself a burning rock, before being exiled from Athens for such an impiety. Newton implicitly sides with the ancient materialist in Rule II.

zh: 规则 III
en: RULE III

zh: 那些不允许增强或减弱程度、且被发现属于实验范围内所有物体的性质，应被视为所有物体的普遍性质。

children: The qualities of bodies, which admit neither intension nor remission of degrees, and which are found to belong to all bodies within the reach of our experiments, are to be esteemed the universal qualities of all bodies whatsoever.

zh: 科学需要这一规则才能从实验概括。牛顿用摆实验研究动量守恒定律。如果动量守恒在实验中成立，他推断同样适用于月球和行星。阿基米德观察自己入浴时水被排开，推断船只入海也排开一定体积水。
en: Science needs this rule if it is to be able to generalize from experiment. Newton carried out experiments using pendulums to investigate what he formulated as a law of conservation of momentum. If the conservation of momentum applied in experiments, he inferred that the same applied to the Moon and planets. When Archimedes observed water being displaced as he stepped into a bath, he inferred that a ship likewise displaces a volume of water as it slides into the sea.

zh: 规则 IV
en: RULE IV

zh: 在实验哲学中，我们应把通过一般归纳从现象中收集的命题视为准确或非常接近真实，尽管可能想象出相反假设，直到出现其他现象使它们更精确或表明例外。

children: In experimental philosophy we are to look upon propositions collected by general induction from phænomena as accurately or very nearly true, notwithstanding any contrary hypotheses that may be imagined, till such time as other phænomena occur, by which they may either be made more accurate, or liable to exceptions.

zh: 我们必须遵循这一规则，以免归纳论证被假设规避。
en: This rule we must follow that the argument of induction may not be evaded by hypotheses.

zh: 鉴于“假设”一词当前联想，这容易被误解。科学通常被描述为提出假设，然后由观察和实验检验。牛顿为何说“我不做假设”？
en: This is easily misunderstood given the current associations with the word ‘hypothesis’. A common presentation of science is that it advances hypotheses about reality, which are then put to the test of observation and experiment. Why did Newton famously remark that he made no hypotheses?

zh: 在此语境中，他指关于世界必须如何运作的先验假设。例如地球固定在宇宙中心，或力只能通过直接物理接触作用。若坚持其中任何一种，就会规避他在《世界体系》中建立的归纳论证。
en: In this context, he meant a priori assumptions about how the world must work. Instances of this would have been the hypothesis that the Earth is fixed at the centre of the universe, or the hypothesis that forces could only act by direct physical contact. Either of these would, if insisted upon, have resulted in an evasion of the arguments from induction that he builds up in his

zh: 我们稍后探讨“通过假设规避归纳论证”在历史唯物主义中如何引发争议。
en: We will later touch on how ‘evading the argument of induction by hypotheses’ has caused controversy in historical materialism.

zh: 关于力学的一点说明
en: A remark on mechanics

zh: 我们上文说牛顿力学建立在古典力学基础上；在阿基米德部分，我们叙述几何学本身对古人而言是用于建筑的机械艺术。牛顿在《原理》全书中依赖古典几何学。他把方法延伸至微积分，但在研究天体运动时仍以欧几里得为立足点。
en: We said above that Newtonian mechanics rested on the foundation of classical mechanics, and in the section on Archimedes we recounted how geometry itself was for the ancients a mechanical art to be used in architecture. Newton relies throughout the
on classical geometry. He extends its methods towards the calculus, but he relies on Euclid as the place to stand while he studies the movement of worlds.

zh: 他对机械艺术与几何学关系有有趣观察：
en: He makes some interesting observations on the relationship between mechanical arts and geometry:

zh: 描绘直
线和圆是问题，但不是几何问题。这些问题的解决需要力学；几何学展示解决后的应用；几何学的荣耀在于，它仅凭从外部引入的少数原理，便能产生如此多东西。
en: To describe right

lines and circles are problems, but not geometrical problems. The solution of these problems is required from mechanics; and by geometry the use of them, when so solved, is shown; and it is the glory of geometry that from those few principles, brought from without, it is able to produce so many things.

zh: 他说，描绘直线和圆——即绘制或标定——不是几何问题，而是制图师或测量员的机械实践问题。公理化演绎几何学利用这些力学简单结果，展示如何组合它们以“产生如此多东西”。
en: He is saying that describing straight lines and circles, that is to say, describing in the sense of drawing or laying out, is not a problem for geometry. It is a problem for the mechanical practice of the draftsman or the surveyor. Axiomatic and deductive geometry then takes these simple results of mechanics and shows how to compose them to ‘produce so many things’.

zh: 因此几何学建立在机械实践上，无非是普遍力学中准确提出并证明测量艺术的部分。但由于手工技艺主要涉及物体运动，几何学通常归于大小，力学归于运动。在这个意义上，理性力学将成为一门科学：准确提出并证明由任何力产生的运动，以及产生任何运动所需的力。
en: Therefore geometry is founded in mechanical practice, and is nothing but that part of universal mechanics which accurately proposes and demonstrates the art of measuring. But since the manual arts are chiefly conversant in the moving of bodies, it comes to pass that geometry is commonly referred to their magnitudes, and mechanics to their motion. In this sense rational mechanics will be the science of motions resulting from any forces whatsoever, and of the forces required to produce any motions, accurately proposed and demonstrated.

zh: 这门科学研究的是物质物体的运动。他将借助几何学，分析运动及引起运动的力。接下来，他定义了自己以几何方式处理物质与运动时将要使用的术语。
en: The science is to be about the motion of material bodies. It is by geometry that he will analyse the motions and forces which impel motions. He goes on to define the terms he will use in this geometric treatment of matter and motion.

zh: 定义
定义 I
en: DEFINITION I.

zh: 物质的量是同一物质的度量，由密度和体积共同产生。

children: The quantity of matter is the measure of the same, arising from its density and bulk conjunctly.

zh: 因此，密度加倍的空气，在双倍空间中，量是四倍；在三倍空间中，量是六倍。雪、细尘或粉末经压缩或液化而致密，以及所有因任何原因以不同方式致密化的物体，都应如此理解。我在此不考虑任何可能自由渗透物体各部分间隙的介质。今后我无论何处提到物体或质量，都指这个量。它通过每个物体的重量得知；因为重量与它成正比，正如我通过精密摆实验发现的那样，后文将展示。
en: Thus, air of a double density, in a double space, is quadruple in quantity; in a triple space, sextuple in quantity. The same thing is to be understood of snow, and fine dust or powders, that are condensed by compression or liquefaction; and of all bodies that are by any causes whatever differently condensed. I have no regard in this place to a medium, if any such there is, that freely pervades the interstices between the parts of bodies. It is this quantity that I mean hereafter everywhere under the name of body or mass. And the same is known by the weight of each body; for it is proportional to the weight, as I have found by experiments on pendulums, very accurately made, which shall be shewn hereafter.

zh: 他把重量确立为物质度量，并把重量与体积区分。这在经验上显而易见，但在两个重要意义上具有重要意义：
en: He is establishing weight as the measure of matter. He is distinguishing the weight of matter from its volume. This is pretty obvious empirically, but it is nevertheless significant in two important senses:

zh: 1. 他明确把假设的光以太（luminiferous ether）排除在质量之外，提到“一种介质（如果真有的话），它自由渗透物体各部分之间的间隙”。如果这种以太存在，他说它是无质量或非物质的。2. 他主张惯性质量与引力质量等价。虽然直到后来阐述万有引力定律才明显，但他预先提到用摆实验证明。
en: 1. He explicitly excludes the hypothetical luminiferous ether from mass with his allusion to a ‘medium, if any such there is, that freely pervades the interstices between the parts of bodies’. If this ether exists, he says it is massless or immaterial. 2. He is asserting the equivalence of inertial and gravitational mass. Although this will not become apparent until he later states his law of gravitation, he refers forward to the experiments with pendulums by which he demonstrated this.

zh: 定义 II
en: DEFINITION II.

zh: 运动量是同一运动的度量，由速度和物质量共同产生。

children: The quantity of motion is the measure of the same, arising from the velocity and quantity of matter conjunctly.

zh: 整体的运动是各部分运动之和；因此，质量加倍、速度相等时，运动量加倍；在这一质量加倍的物体中，速度也加倍时，运动量为四倍。
en: The motion of the whole is the sum of the motions of all the parts; and therefore in a body double in quantity, with equal velocity, the motion is double; with twice the velocity, it is quadruple.

zh: 牛顿所说的运动即我们现在所说的动量，因此他用文字给出定义方程
。《原理》中还没有独立动能概念。我们稍后回到这一点。
en: What Newton called motion is what we now call momentum, so he is giving in words the defining equation
. There is no distinct concept of kinetic energy yet present in the
. We return to this later.

zh: 定义 IV
en: DEFINITION IV.

zh: 外力是作用于物体以改变其状态的作用，无论是静止状态还是沿直线匀速运动状态。

children: An impressed force is an action exerted upon a body, in order to change its state, either of rest, or of moving uniformly forward in a right line.

zh: 这是定性定义，由定律I 和II 赋予定量意义。它在很大程度上依赖定律获得含义。这是以下内容的引子：
en: This is a qualitative definition that is given quantitative meaning by his Laws I & II lower down. It does, however, depend in large part on the laws for its meaning. It is a prelude to:

zh: 定义 V
en: DEFINITION V.

zh: 向心力是使物体被吸引、推动或以任何方式趋向作为中心的某一点的力。

children: A centripetal force is that by which bodies are drawn or impelled, or any way tend, towards a point as to a centre.

zh: 这里他首次把方向性引入力。有趣的是，在定义IV 中力还不是向量，没有方向性。引入方向性时，他特指向心吸引力。可能由于未引入参考系，他认为无法定义方向性。一个点允许定义朝向该点的方向性，也允许定义远离该点的力——离心力。全书大部分，牛顿谨慎处理不同力律，考虑与距离成反比、与距离平方成反比、与距离立方成反比等。令人惊讶的是，他把定义限制在吸引力，而未定义排斥力。即使当时未研究静电斥力，磁斥力已被研究。
en: Here he introduces, for the first time, directionality to force. It is interesting that prior to this, in Definition IV, force is not yet a vector, not yet having directionality. When he introduces directionality, it is in the specific sense of a centripetal attractive force. It is possible that absent any introduction of a frame of reference, he felt it impossible to define directionality. One point allows directionality to be defined towards that point, but it also allows the definition of a force away from the point – centrifugal. In most of the book, Newton is careful to deal with different kinds of force laws, considering laws that vary inversely with distance, inversely with square of distance, cube of distance etc. It is surprising that he restricts the definitions to attractive ones rather than defining repulsive ones as well. Even if the repulsive electrostatic force was not studied in his day, repulsive magnetism was.

zh: 定义 III
en: DEFINITION III.

zh: vis insita（内在力），或物质固有力量，是抵抗的力量，每个物体凭此尽力保持当前状态，无论是静止还是沿直线匀速运动。

children: The vis insita, or innate force of matter, is a power of resisting, by which every body, as much as in it lies, endeavours to persevere in its present state, whether it be of rest, or of moving uniformly forward in a right line.

zh: 他定性定义惯性质量。然而在当今公认的牛顿力学表述中，惯性不会被描述为力。
en: He is here defining in a qualitative way the notion of inertial mass. However, in what is now the accepted presentation of Newtonian mechanics, inertia would not be described as a force.

zh: 他还有三个定义（VI–VIII）给出量化向心力的不同方式。第一个定义为“与从中心通过周围空间传播它的原因的效力成正比”，这有些晦涩，因为不清楚如何衡量原因效力及单位。下一个定义把向心力的加速度量定义为与单位时间诱导速度成正比。在
关系中，这相当于忽略被加速物体的惯性质量，在处理围绕大质量物体运行的不同小质量时完全合理。此时测量引力的“加速度量”等同于我们现在所说的引力场强度：牛顿每千克。他最后把向心力的动力量定义为与给定时间产生的运动成正比。他用“运动”指动量
，因此似乎指以千克米每秒平方为单位的量。
en: He has three definitions (VI to VIII) giving different ways of quantifying centripetal force. The first defines it as ‘proportional to the efficacy of the cause that propagates it from the centre, through the spaces round about’, which is rather obscure since it is not clear how one is to measure the efficacy of a cause or in what units he intends to measure it. The next defines the accelerative quantity of centripetal forces as being proportional to the velocity they induce per unit time. In the

relation, this amounts to abstracting from the inertial mass of the body being accelerated, something which is perfectly reasonable when dealing with different small masses in orbit around a much larger one. In this case, measuring the ‘accelerative quantity’ of the gravitational force is equivalent to what we now term the intensity of the gravitational field: newtons per kilogram. He finally defines the motive quantity of a centripetal force as proportional to the
it generates in a given time. He uses the term
for what we would now term momentum (
), so he appears to mean something that in SI units would be measured in kilogram metres per second squared.

zh: 时间与空间
“物体与虚空”概念对古典原子论至关重要。对牛顿而言，任何关于物体运动的系统理论都必须先有时间和空间的概念定义。他对时间和空间的定义被广泛引用，因为正是在这一问题上，后爱因斯坦物理学与他分歧。
en: The conceptual pair (bodies, void) was fundamental to classical atomism. For Newton, a conceptual definition of time and space had to precede any systematic theory of the motion of bodies. His definitions of time and space are widely quoted because it is on this issue that post-Einstein physics departs from him.

zh: 时间
en: TIME

zh: 绝对的、真实的、数学的时间，就其自身和本性而言，均匀流逝，与任何外部事物无关，又名持续时间；相对的、表观的、普通的时间，是借助运动对持续时间作出的一种可感知的外部度量（无论准确还是不均匀），通常用来代替真实时间；例如一小时、一天、一月、一年。
en: Absolute, true, and mathematical time, of itself, and from its own nature flows equably without regard to anything external, and by another name is called duration: relative, apparent, and common time, is some sensible and external (whether accurate or unequable) measure of duration by the means of motion, which is commonly used instead of true time; such as an hour, a day, a month, a year.

zh: 牛顿在此使用隐喻：绝对时间流动。但比喻虽合理，却自相矛盾。溪流流动时在运动，其运动在时间语境中定义。
en: Newton here applies a metaphor: that absolute time flows. But plausible as the metaphor seems, it is surely contradictory. When a stream flows, it moves. Its motion is defined in the context of time.

zh: 我们把树枝扔进桥一侧；几秒后它出现在另一侧，于是得出河水流动。但测量流动需要两个不同时间观察。在
，树枝落入河流；在
秒，我们看到树枝从桥另一侧下游4 米处浮出。于是水流速度为每秒半米。
en: We throw a twig down one side of a bridge; a few seconds later, it appears on the other side, and we then conclude that the river flows. But to measure the flow, we need two observations at distinct times. At time
, the twig lands in the stream, and at time
seconds, we see the twig emerge, 4 metres downstream on the other side of the bridge. So we conclude that the water is flowing at half a metre per second.

zh: 这是空间相对于时间的流动。但时间相对于什么流动？
en: This is a flow in space with respect to time. But what is time supposed to flow with respect to?

zh: 谈论“时间流动”在逻辑上与谈论“空间距离流动”一样无意义。
en: To speak of the flow of time makes no more logical sense than it would to speak of spatial distance flowing.

zh: 如果绘制
，可以说曲线相对于x 轴向上流动，并求导数
，它告诉我y 随x 变化向上流动多快。但我能这样做，因为涉及两个正交维度。类似地，对下落物体方程
及导数
，可确定物体在时间t 的空间向下流动。这同样因为方程中时间是正交维度。但时间不能相对于自身流动。
en: If I plot a graph for
, I can say that the line flows upwards with respect to the
axis, and I can take the derivative of this,
, which tells me how fast
flows up as
changes. But I can only do these things because two orthogonal dimensions are involved. Similarly, given an analogous equation of motion for a falling body,
and its derivative
, I can determine the downward flow through space of the object at time
. Again, this is because time, in the equation, is an orthogonal dimension. But time cannot flow with respect to itself.

zh: 但他刚引入流动的绝对时间，就把它搁置，引入实际使用的相对时间。
en: But he no sooner introduces his flowing absolute time than he puts it to one side to introduce what he actually works with – relative time.

zh: 他所说的可感或相对时间由运动衡量，例如年或小时。这些确实由运动衡量：一年是地球绕太阳公转，一天是地球自转。到牛顿时代，人类工艺已制造钟表，其运动模拟地球运动，地球自转一圈时针转两圈。
en: His sensible or relative time is measured by motions, giving as examples units like the year or the hour. These are indeed measured by motions: the motion of the Earth around the Sun for the year and the spin of the Earth on its axis for the day. By Newton’s day, human arts had constructed clocks whose motions modelled those of the Earth, with two rotations of the hour hand for each rotation of the Earth.

zh: 据牛顿，运动不能以绝对时间为参照测量，只能相对于其他运动测量。在天文学中，古典天文学家通过测量恒星或参考星相对于天顶的角度，确定月球掩恒星的时刻。
en: According to Newton, motion cannot be measured in relation to absolute time. Instead, it can only be measured in relation to other motions. In the field of astronomy, a classical astronomer would determine the moment of occultation of a star by the Moon by measuring the angle with respect to the celestial zenith of either the same star or a reference star.

zh: 然后转换为恒星时
记录。牛顿旨在解释行星运动，在没有独立时间尺度时观察运动与位置相关性。他认为所有运动在概念上相对于时间定义，形成时间维度。地球以绝对时间为基准自转，月球绕地球角运动。牛顿从稳定比例存在推断，这些不同旋转有共同、绝对、客观的时间维度。
en: The astronomer could then convert this to sidereal time

for their records. Newton aimed to explain planetary motion, observing correlations of motions and positions without an independent measure of time. He believed that all motions are conceptually defined with respect to time, creating a time dimension. The Earth rotates with absolute time, while the Moon has an angular rotation around us. Newton inferred from the existence of stable ratios that there is a common absolute objective time dimension for these varied rotations.

zh: 空间
en: SPACE

zh: 绝对空间，就其本性而言，与任何外部事物无关，始终相似且不动。相对空间是绝对空间的某种可移动维度或度量；我们的感官通过其相对于物体的位置确定它；通常被当作不动空间；例如地下、空中或天体空间的维度，由相对于地球的位置决定。
en: Absolute space, in its own nature, without regard to anything external, remains always similar and immovable. Relative space is some movable dimension or measure of the absolute spaces; which our senses determine by its position to bodies; and which is vulgarly taken for immovable space; such is the dimension of a subterraneous, an æreal, or celestial space, determined by its position in respect of the Earth.

zh: 牛顿假设的绝对空间在20 世纪物理学中随相对论被抛弃。但他刚提出绝对空间，就转向相对空间。他知道并接受伽利略相对性：在匀速运动的参考系中，运动定律不变。
en: Newton’s hypothesized absolute space is something that was dropped by twentieth-century physics with the theory of relativity. But no sooner has Newton raised the idea of absolute space than he immediately moves on to relative space. He was aware of and accepted Galilean relativity, which is to say that the laws of motion remain the same in a constantly moving frame of reference.

zh: 他后来用船的例子阐述：
en: He later elaborates on this relativity, giving the example of a ship:

zh: 我们从船实验得到明确证明；无论船静止还是沿直线匀速前进，所有运动以相同方式发生。
en: A clear proof of which we have from the experiment of a ship; where all motions happen after the same manner, whether the ship is at rest, or is carried uniformly forwards in a right line.

zh: 但既然接受伽利略相对性，为何坚持绝对空间？我们认为理由在他对运动的定义最后部分。
en: But given that he accepts Galilean relativity, why does he persist with the notion of absolute space? The rationale, we think, is provided in the last section of his definition of motion.

zh: 运动
en: MOTION

zh: 绝对运动是物体从一个绝对位置向另一个绝对位置的平移；相对运动是从一个相对位置向另一个相对位置的平移。因此在航行船上，物体的相对位置是它占据的船体部分，或它填充的船舱部分，因此随船移动；相对静止是物体持续位于船的同一部分或船舱同一部分。但真实绝对静止是物体持续位于不可移动空间的同一部分，而船本身、船舱及其中一切都在该空间中运动。因此，如果地球确实静止，船上相对静止的物体将以船在地球上的相同速度真实绝对运动。但如果地球也运动，物体真实绝对运动将部分来自地球在不可移动空间中的真实运动，部分来自船在地球上的相对运动；如果物体在船内也相对运动，其真实运动将部分来自地球在不可移动空间中的真实运动，部分来自船在地球上的相对运动。假设地球上船所在部分以10010 份速度向东运动；船本身在强风满帆下以10 份速度向西航行；一名水手在船上以所述速度的1份向东行走；那么水手在不可移动空间中以10001 份速度真实向东移动，而在地球上以9 份速度相对向西移动。
en: Absolute motion is the translation of a body from one absolute place into another; and relative motion, the translation from one relative place into another. Thus in a ship under sail, the relative place of a body is that part of the ship which the body possesses; or that part of its cavity which the body fills, and which therefore moves together with the ship: and relative rest is the continuance of the body in the same part of the ship, or of its cavity. But real, absolute rest, is the continuance of the body in the same part of that immovable space, in which the ship itself, its cavity and all that it contains, is moved. Wherefore, if the Earth is really at rest, the body, which relatively rests in the ship, will really and absolutely move with the same velocity which the ship has on the Earth. But if the Earth also moves, the true and absolute motion of the body will arise, partly from the true motion of the Earth, in immovable space; partly from the relative motion of the ship on the Earth; and if the body moves also relatively in the ship; its true motion will arise, partly from the true motion of the Earth, in immovable space, and partly from the relative motions as well of the ship on the Earth. As if that part of the Earth, where the ship is, was truly moved toward the east, with a velocity of 10010 parts; while the ship itself, with a fresh gale, and full sails, is carried towards the west, with a velocity expressed by 10 of those parts; but a sailor walks in the ship towards the east, with 1 part of the said velocity; then the sailor will be moved truly in immovable space towards the east, with a velocity of 10001 parts, and relatively on the Earth towards the west, with a velocity of 9 of those parts.
body.review: 此段底本在物体也相对于船运动的分句中，仍只列地球与船的运动，表述有所脱落；后面的水手算例明确计入了水手相对于船的速度。译文保留底本而不擅补引文。

zh: 但他接着解释为何既存在绝对运动又存在相对运动。
en: But he goes on to explain his belief as to why there is such a thing as absolute motion as well as relative motion.

zh: 但我们可以通过性质、原因和效果区分静止与运动、绝对与相对。静止的性质是：真正静止的物体彼此确实静止。因此，尽管在遥远恒星区域或更远处可能存在绝对静止物体；但仅凭我们区域内物体相对位置，无法知道其中任何一个是否与那个遥远物体保持相同位置；因此绝对静止不能由我们区域内物体位置确定。
en: But we may distinguish rest and motion, absolute and relative, one from the other by their properties, causes and effects. It is a property of rest, that bodies really at rest do rest in respect to one another. And therefore as it is possible, that in the remote regions of the fixed stars, or perhaps far beyond them, there may be some body absolutely at rest; but impossible to know, from the position of bodies to one another in our regions whether any of these do keep the same position to that remote body; it follows that absolute rest cannot be determined from the position of bodies in our regions.

zh: 区分绝对与相对运动的效果，是远离圆周运动轴心的离心力。因为纯粹相对圆周运动中没有这种力，但真实绝对圆周运动中有，大小取决于运动量。

children: The effects which distinguish absolute from relative motion are, the forces of receding from the axis of circular motion. For there are no such forces in a circular motion purely relative, but in a true and absolute circular motion, they are greater or less, according to the quantity of the motion.

zh: 最后一点非常重要。
en: The final point above is very important.

zh: 绝对平移已被迈克尔逊–莫雷实验否定，但牛顿已指出，除旋转外绝对空间不可测量。他通过思想实验证明：用绳子把半桶水悬挂在树上。水最初静止，桶旋转后运动传给水，水开始旋转。水面两侧向上弯曲，表明水最初相对于绝对空间未旋转。桶壁约束产生向心力，使水在边缘堆积。
en: Absolute translation is discredited by the Michaelson-Morely experiment, but Newton was already saying that absolute space is immeasurable except for rotation. This is proven through a thought experiment. He demonstrates that absolute space is immeasurable except for rotation by hanging a half-filled bucket with water from a tree with a rope. The water initially remains stationary, but as the bucket spins, its motion is transmitted to the water, which starts spinning. This causes the water’s surface to curve up at the sides, indicating that the water was not initially spinning with respect to absolute space. The constraint of the bucket wall creates a centripetal force, causing the water to pile up at the edges.
body.review: 本书英文将实验名拼作 Michaelson-Morely；中文按通常译名“迈克尔逊—莫雷”处理，英文照录。这里关于绝对空间和水桶实验的推论属于原作者论述。

zh: 这个思想实验很有说服力。
en: This thought experiment is quite convincing.

zh: 定律
他的运动定律为自然法则树立标准。此前已有阿基米德浮体排水定律和伽利略加速度定律
，但此前没有哲学家提出完整运动定律。
en: His laws of motion set the standard for what we understand natural laws to be. There had been previous formulations – Archimedes law of displacement by floating bodies, and Galileo’s law of acceleration
– but no previous philosopher had formulated a complete set of motion laws.

zh: 每个物体都保持静止状态或沿直线匀速运动状态，除非施加于它的力迫使它改变这一状态。
en: Every body perseveres in its state of rest, or of uniform motion in a right line, unless it is compelled to change that state by forces impressed thereon.

zh: 运动量的改变始终与施加的驱动力成正比，并沿该力施加的直线方向发生。
en: The alteration of motion is ever proportional to the motive force impressed and is made in the direction of the right line in which that force is impressed.

zh: 对每个作用，总有一个大小相等、方向相反的反作用；或者说，两个物体彼此之间的相互作用总是大小相等、方向相反。
en: To every action, there is always opposed an equal reaction, or the mutual actions of two bodies upon each other are always equal and directed to contrary parts.

zh: 如果你用手指压石头，手指也被石头压。如果马拉绳子系着的石头，马（如果可以这么说）也被同样向石头方向拉回：因为拉伸的绳子努力恢复原状，会把马向石头方向拉，与把石头向马方向拉一样多，并阻碍一方前进，恰如促进另一方前进。
en: If you press a stone with your finger, the finger is also pressed by the stone. If a horse draws a stone tied to a rope, the horse (if I may so say) will be equally drawn back towards the stone: for the distended rope, by the same endeavour to relax or unbend itself, will draw the horse as much towards the stone as it does the stone towards the horse, and will obstruct the progress of the one as much as it advances that of the other.

zh: 定律III 是明确等价关系，建立在阿基米德力学等价关系上。牛顿用手指压石头例子重申伽利略更有限的观点：
en: Law III is a clear equivalence relation. As such, it builds on the equivalence relations of Archimidean mechanics. With his example of the pressure of a finger on a stone, Newton is repeating a more limited point made by Galileo

zh: 当人手持石头时，他所做的难道不是施加向上推力［virtù impellente］，其大小等于重力向下拉石头的力量［facoltà］吗？只要你握住石头，难道不是持续施加这种力［virtù］吗？
en: When one holds a stone in his hand does he do anything but give it a force impelling [virtù impellente] it upwards equal to the power [facoltà] of gravity drawing it downwards? And do you not continuously impress this force [virtù] upon the stone as long as you hold it in the hand?

zh: 伽利略只在物体与重力平衡的特殊情况给出作用反作用等式。牛顿把它扩展为运动和加速物体的普遍原理，无论力性质如何。
en: Galileo only gave this equality of action and reaction in the special case of a body balanced against gravity. Newton extended it to a general principle of moving and accelerating bodies, irrespective of the nature of the forces acting on them.

zh: 牛顿首次提出变化和运动力学，其中所有变化和运动都受普遍等价关系和约束支配，这些关系可用数学处理。在牛顿那里，与阿基米德和伽利略一样，数学处理主要基于古典几何。他的文本不断穿插几何图示，以说明其论证。论述力合成时，他写道：
en: Newton is the first to present mechanics of change and motion in which all the changes and motions are subject to certain universal equivalences and constraints, equivalences and constraints which can be treated mathematically. In Newton’s case, as with Archimedes and Galileo, the mathematical treatment is still mainly in terms of classical geometry. His text is constantly interspersed with geometric diagrams to illustrate its arguments. Dealing with the composition of forces, he writes:

zh: 物体在两个力共同作用下，会在同一时间内描绘出平行四边形的对角线；这段时间正是两个力分别作用时，物体描绘出相应边所需的时间。
en: A body by two forces conjoined will describe the diagonal of a parallelogram, in the same time that it would describe the sides, by those forces apart.

zh: 原书无编号插图：力的平行四边形合成示意。
A、B、C、D为原图顶点标记。
en: Unnumbered diagram: parallelogram composition of forces.
body.review: 此图在原书中没有编号和图注；此处说明为编者补充。

zh: 由此解释任意一个直线力AD 由两个斜向力AC 和CD 合成；反之，任意直线力AD 分解为两个斜向力AC 和CD。这种合成与分解在力学中得到充分验证。
en: And hence is explained the composition of any one direct force AD, out of any two oblique forces AC and CD; and, on the contrary, the resolution of any one direct force AD into two oblique forces AC and CD: which composition and resolution are abundantly confirmed from mechanics.

zh: 他提出明确守恒定律。首先是动量守恒：
en: He formulates a set of explicit conservation laws. First, a conservation of momentum law:

zh: 运动量——通过取指向相同方向的运动之和，并取指向相反方向的运动之差而得到——在物体相互作用中不变。
en: The quantity of motion, which is collected by taking the sum of the motions directed towards the same parts, and the difference of those that are directed to contrary parts, suffers no change from the action of bodies among themselves.

zh: 这是守恒定律：物体集合的总动量守恒，由定律推导。回顾牛顿所说的“运动”是
，即速度与质量乘积，现在称为动量。他的意思是：对一组物体，若选择任意方向并计算它们在该方向的动量之和，那么物体间任何相互作用，无论相互引力还是碰撞，都不能改变该方向总动量。
en: The above is a conservation law – conservation of aggregate momentum of a collection of bodies – deduced from the laws. Recall that by ‘motion’, Newton means

, the product of velocity and mass in motion, what we would now call momentum. He is saying that given a collection of bodies, if you choose an arbitrary direction and compute the sum of their momenta in that direction, then no interaction of those bodies, whether mutual gravitation or impacts between them, can alter the aggregate momentum of the bodies in the specified direction.

zh: 他随后推广到重心。他论证，两个或多个物体的共同重心无论它们如何作用都保持不变，确保所有相互作用物体，排除外部作用和阻碍，要么静止，要么沿直线匀速运动。此外，两个相互作用物体系统中，它们相对于共同重心的相对运动，无论接近还是远离，由于物体之间的相互距离而相等。
en: He next extends this to their centres of gravity. He argues that the common centre of gravity of two or more bodies remains constant regardless of their actions, ensuring that all bodies acting upon each other, excluding outward actions and impediments, are either at rest or moving uniformly in a right line. Moreover in a system of two bodies acting on each other, their relative motions, whether approaching or receding from the common centre of gravity, will be equal due to reciprocal distances between the bodies.
body.review: 底本此段将重心“保持不变”与系统匀速运动并列，又称相对运动“相等”，措辞不够严谨。译文照录作者论述；在无外力时应区分质心匀速运动、各物体速度与各自运动量，不能把这些量混为一谈。

zh: 这把阿基米德重心研究扩展到通过相互作用力相互影响的运动物体，后来用于行星轨道问题。例如，这意味着月球绕地球公转时，地月重心不变。他小心限定于物体“相互作用”的效果，因为地球和月球嵌入太阳引力场时，该场影响会改变地月共同重心。
en: This extends Archimedes’ work on centres of gravity to moving bodies interacting by mutual forces. This will later be used to deal with problems of planetary orbits. It means, for instance, that the centre of gravity of the Earth and the Moon is not altered as the Moon orbits the Earth. He is careful to restrict this to the effect of the bodies ‘acting upon each other’, since to the extent that the Earth and Moon are embedded in a solar gravitational field, the effect of this will alter the mutual centre of gravity of the Earth-Moon system.

zh: 在给定空间内，物体运动彼此相同，无论该空间静止还是沿直线匀速前进且无圆周运动。
en: The motions of bodies included in a given space are the same among themselves, whether that space is at rest, or moves uniformly forwards in a right line without any circular motion.

zh: 我们从船实验得到明确证明；无论船静止还是沿直线匀速前进，所有运动以相同方式发生。
en: A clear proof of which we have from the experiment of a ship; where all motions happen after the same manner, whether the ship is at rest, or is carried uniformly forwards in a right line.

zh: 由于地球和月球绕太阳公转时并非“无圆周运动沿直线匀速前进”，他明确把行星–卫星系统排除在规则外。但更广泛地，他主张如今所称的伽利略相对性：惯性参考系中物体相对运动不受参考系匀速运动影响。船的比喻源自伽利略。
en: Since, in orbiting the Sun, the Earth and Moon do not move ‘uniformly forward in a right line without any circular motion’, he is explicitly excluding planet-satellite systems from his rule that the ‘motions of the bodies are the same among themselves’. But more generally, he is asserting what is now known as Gallilean relativity – that is to say that the mutual motions of bodies in an inertial frame of reference are unaffected by the uniform motion of that frame of reference. The analogy with a ship is borrowed from Gallileo.

zh: 牛顿明确排除圆周运动，因为在他看来，这种圆周运动通过空间区分相对与绝对运动。他援引伽利略：下落物体经过距离与时间平方成正比：
en: Newton explicitly excludes circular motion since according to him such circular motion distinguishes relative from absolute motion through space. He explicitly refers to Galilleo for authority on the fact that falling bodies traverse a distance proportional to the square of their time of fall:

zh: 根据前两条定律和前两个推论，伽利略发现物体下落遵循时间平方比，抛射体运动呈抛物线；经验与二者相符，除非运动因空气阻力略延迟。当物体下落时，均匀重力在相等时间施加相等力，因此产生相等的速度增量；整个时间施加总力，产生与时间成正比的总速度。成比例时间内描述的距离与速度和时间乘积成正比，即与时间平方成正比。
en: By the first two Laws and the first two Corollaries, Galileo discovered that the descent of bodies observed the duplicate ratio of the time, and that the motion of projectiles was in the curve of a parabola; experience agreeing with both, unless so far as these motions are a little retarded by the resistance of the air. When a body is falling, the uniform force of its gravity acting equally, impresses, in equal particles of time, equal forces upon that body, and therefore generates equal velocities; and in the whole time impresses a whole force, and generates a whole velocity proportional to the time. And the spaces described in proportional times are as the velocities and the times conjunctly; that is, in a duplicate ratio of the times.

zh: 这里的关系是
和
。随后，他叙述了自己用充作摆锤的钢球相互碰撞所进行的实际实验，以验证这些关系，并仔细计入空气阻力的影响。
en: The relations here are
and
. He then recounts actual experiments he has undertaken with steel balls as pendulums that collide to verify the relations, with careful allowance being made for the effects of air resistance.
body.review: 底本此处印作d≈t²，但前文文字说距离与时间平方成正比；比例关系通常写为d∝t²。

zh: 他证明引力的方法

children: His method of proof of gravity

zh: 基于运动基本定律，牛顿在《原理》第一卷考察不同力作用下物体的多种可能轨迹。他不仅研究平方反比力，事实上直到第三卷才引入万有引力定律。他从初始运动定律推导不同力下预期轨道和轨迹，得出概括：
en: From the basic laws of motion, Newton in book I of the

examines many possible trajectories of bodies interacting under different types of forces. He does not only look at inverse square law forces like his law of gravitation. Indeed, he does not introduce the law of gravitation until book III. He instead deduces from his initial laws of motion what orbits and trajectories would be expected under different sorts of forces. He comes up with the following generalizations:

zh: 如果周期与半径成正比，因此速度相等，向心力与半径成反比；反之亦然。
en: If the periodic times are as the radii, and therefore the velocities equal, the centripetal forces will be reciprocally as the radii; and the contrary.

zh: 如果周期与半径的3/2 次方成正比
，因此速度与半径的平方根成反比
，向心力与半径平方成反比；反之亦然。
en: If the periodic times are in the
ratio of the radii,
and therefore the velocities reciprocally in the subduplicate ratio of the radii,
the centripetal forces will be in the duplicate ratio of the radii inversely, and the contrary.

zh: 一般说来，如果周期与半径
的任意幂
成正比，因而速度与半径的幂
成反比，那么向心力就与半径的幂
成反比；反之亦然。
en: And universally, if the periodic time is as any power
of the radius
, and therefore the velocity reciprocally as the power
of the radius, the centripetal force will be reciprocally as the power
of the radius; and the contrary.

zh: 他现在有把轨道周期与力性质联系的普遍规则，还能推导开普勒等面积定律作为向心力平方反比时的特例。第三卷引入六个关键事实，即“现象”：
en: He now has a general rule which relates orbital periods to the nature of forces. He is also able to deduce Kepler’s law that orbital bodies sweep equal areas in equal times as a special case that holds if centripetal forces have an inverse square law. In book III, he introduces six key facts, or, as he puts them, Phænomena:

zh: 1. 木星卫星轨道周期与其轨道半径的3/2 次方成正比。2. 土星卫星轨道周期同样与轨道半径的3/2 次方成正比。3. 五大行星——水星、金星、火星、木星、土星——绕太阳公转。4. 它们的周期与到太阳平均距离的3/2 次方成比例。5. 虽然行星以连接太阳与行星的线段为向径扫过面积与时间成正比，但连接行星与地球的半径扫过面积无此关系。6. 月球以连接地球中心与月球的线段为向径扫过面积与时间成正比。
en: 1. That the orbital periods of the moons of Jupiter are in
ratio to their orbital radii. 2. That the orbital periods of the moons of Saturn are similarly in

ratio to their orbital radii. 3. That the five primary planets: Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn rotate around the Sun. 4. That they have periodic times in sequiduplicate proportion of their mean distances from the Sun. 5. That while the areas which the planets describe by radii drawn to the Sun are proportional to the times of description, no such relation exists in the areas that are swept by radii connecting the planets to the Earth. 6. That the Moon, by a radius drawn to the Earth’s centre, describes an area proportional to the time of description.

zh: 所有情况他都引用当时最佳轨道半径和周期估计。基于这些现象和先前轨道周期结果，他推断木星卫星、主要行星和月球都必须受平方反比力作用而偏离直线运动。他得出结论：
en: In all cases, he cites what were then the best-known estimates of orbital radii and periods to justify his claims. From these phenomena and his previous results about orbital periods, he deduces that the moons of Jupiter, the primary planets and the Moon must all be drawn of rectilinear motion by a force subject to an inverse square law. He concludes
body.review: 底本作drawn of rectilinear motion，疑漏一个f；中文依本段轨道论证译为“偏离直线运动”，英文保留底本。

zh: 迄今把天体束缚在轨道上的力被称为向心力；但既然已明确它只能是引力，今后称之为重力。
en: The force which retains the celestial bodies in their orbits has been hitherto called centripetal force; but it being now made plain that it can be no other than a gravitating force, we shall hereafter call it gravity.

zh: 他随后论证引力不仅与距离平方成反比，还与物体质量成正比，无论物体被吸向哪一个天体。他的论证是：若木星及其卫星所受太阳引力与质量不成正比，木星卫星轨道会明显被太阳引力扭曲，但事实并非如此。最终表述为：引力与质量成正比，与距离平方成反比。
en: He then argues that this gravitational force must not only operate inversely to the square of distances but must also operate in proportion to the masses of the bodies, irrespective of the body towards which the bodies are drawn. His proof is that were it the case that the gravitational attraction towards the Sun experienced by Jupiter and its satellites was not in proportion to their masses, then the orbits of Jupiter’s moons would be very evidently distorted by the Sun’s gravity, which is not the case. His final formulation is a law of attraction that is proportional to the masses and inversely as the square of distances.

zh: 回顾整个论证结构：
en: Recapitulating the whole structure of the argument,

zh: 首先陈述经实验验证的运动定律。
en: He initially states laws of motion that have been verified by experiment.

zh: 通过冗长几何证明，阐明符合这些定律及各种可设想力律的可能轨迹。
en: He then, by lengthy geometrical proofs, demonstrates the possible trajectories consistent with these laws of motion and various conceivable force laws.

zh: 从当时所有可见卫星和行星观测，证明它们遵循平方反比引力推导的轨道。
en: From observation of all the moons and planets then visible, he shows that these follow the trajectories that would follow from inverse square attraction.

deduces what the experimental method, which calls itself philosophy, undertakes to know falsely and with unfelicitous success from experiments, seeking as it does with blind zeal and by means of the senses the simulacrum of the true concepts of philosophy.

zh: 黑格尔批评牛顿为证明惯性质量与引力质量相等而做的摆实验。
黑格尔声称牛顿只证明不同物体重量相等。他完全忽略实验要点：我们没有先验理由认为作为重量的引力质量应等于惯性质量，即对加速度的抵抗。二者相同是经验事实，但并非必然。
en: Hegel criticizes the experiments Newton conducted with pendulums to establish the equality of inertial and gravitational mass.
Hegel claims that all that Newton has done is show that the weights of different bodies are equal. Hegel completely misses the point of the experiments, that is, that we have no

reason to assume that gravitational mass as weight should equal inertial mass: resistance to acceleration. It is an empirical fact that the two are the same, but it does not necessarily have to be the case.

zh: 物理学家推测“暗物质”有惯性质量，但仅通过引力与普通物质相互作用。反之，若牛顿错了，有惯性质量的带电粒子可能通过静电力而非引力与普通物质相互作用。但这些粒子存在仍是未解经验问题。牛顿摆实验验证引力质量与惯性质量等价，是历史序列中一环。
en: Physicists speculate that ‘dark matter’ has inertial mass but only interacts with ordinary matter through gravity. Conversely, charged particles with inertial mass could, if Newton was wrong, interact with ordinary matter through electrostatic force, but not via gravity. However, the existence of these particles is still an unanswered empirical question. Newton’s pendulum experiments, which verified the equivalence of gravitational and inertial masses, sit in a historical sequence of such tests.

zh: 牛顿时代已知除引力外的力，如通过砝码或弹簧秤测量的绳索张力。牛顿用引力做摆实验，但也可用钟表摆轮。摆轮依靠弹簧力与轮质量对抗设定振荡周期。
en: Forces other than gravity were known in Newton’s time, such as the tension on a cord measured by weight or a spring balance. Newton experimented with pendulums using gravitational force, but clock balance wheels could have been used. They rely on the force of a spring working against the mass of the wheel to set the period of oscillation.

zh: 一位在概念分析方面有黑格尔声誉的哲学家，竟完全未理解重量与惯性质量的概念区别，这告诉我们一些东西。
en: That a philosopher with Hegel’s repute for conceptual analysis should have so completely failed to understand the conceptual distinction between weight and inertial mass tells us something.
